chunks: From him, from Abu Abdillah, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from Umayyah ibn Amr, from al-Sha'iri, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a ship that broke apart in the sea; some of its cargo was retrieved by divers, and the sea itself brought out some of what had sunk in it. He said: 'As for what the sea brought out, it belongs to its owners, for God brought it out. And as for what was retrieved by divers, it belongs to them, and they have more right to it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on ownership of shipwrecked cargo recovered by divers versus that washed ashore?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between *al-kasb* (acquisition through effort) and *al-tabi‘* (natural occurrence) in maritime law. It establishes that naturally washed-up cargo retains original ownership, while divers’ property rights are derived from their active labor, reflecting the Shia principle that effort confers a stronger claim to found goods.
